record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: How does the intelligence order relation compare, both theoretically and on restricted problem classes, to conventional IQ tests and other intelligence or performance measures, and does narrowing the order relation to specific classes of environments reveal principled connections between apparently different domain-specific performance metrics?

evidence.quote: a) General and specific performance measures. Currently it is only partially understood how the IOR theoretically compares to the myriad of other tests of intelligence such as conventional IQ tests or even other performance tests proposed by AI other researchers. Another open question is whether the IOR might in some sense be too general. One may narrow the IOR to specific classes of problems [LH04b] and compare how the resulting IOR measures compare to standard performance measures for each problem class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let an agent be a (possibly stochastic) policy π that, at each time step t = 1, 2, …, receives an observation o_t and reward r_t ∈ [0,1] from an environment μ and outputs an action a_t. An environment μ is a computable conditional probability measure over observation–reward sequences given action sequences. Let E denote a class of such environments, and for each μ ∈ E let

   V^π_μ := E_μ[ Σ_{t=1}^∞ γ_t · r_t ],

where (γ_t) is a fixed nonnegative summable discount sequence. For a chosen prior w : E → (0,1] with Σ_μ w(μ) ≤ 1, define the universal value

   Υ(π; E, w) := Σ_{μ ∈ E} w(μ) · V^π_μ.

The Intelligence Order Relation (IOR) on agents (relative to (E, w)) is the preorder

   π ⪰_{E,w} π'   ⇔   Υ(π; E, w) ≥ Υ(π'; E, w),

with strict version ≻_{E,w}. When E is the class of all lower-semicomputable chronological environments and w(μ) = 2^{-K(μ)} (Kolmogorov complexity prior), call ⪰_{E,w} the universal IOR.

Problem. Provide a rigorous comparative analysis of the IOR and other measures of agent performance:

(1) (General comparison.) Determine the formal relationship between the universal IOR ⪰_{E,w} and standard human-intelligence tests modeled as score functions S : Agents → ℝ (e.g., IQ-style batteries formalized as finite collections of task-environments with weighted scoring). Specifically, does there exist a choice of (E, w) such that ⪰_{E,w} agrees, up to a monotone transformation, with a given score function S on a prescribed class of agents? Characterize necessary and sufficient conditions on S for such an (E, w) to exist.

(2) (Restriction to subclasses.) For natural restricted environment classes E' ⊂ E — for instance, finite-state Markov decision processes, fully observable deterministic environments, sequence-prediction environments, ergodic environments, or bandit problems — identify the resulting restricted IOR ⪰_{E', w'} and prove whether it coincides with, refines, or is incomparable to the canonical performance metrics used for that class (e.g., expected cumulative regret for bandits, average reward for ergodic MDPs, log-loss for sequence prediction). In each case, exhibit either an equivalence theorem (the restricted IOR induces the same total preorder on agents as the standard metric) or a separation (a pair of agents ordered oppositely by the two preorders).

(3) (Principled unification.) Decide whether varying E' across a family of subclasses yields a principled hierarchy of performance measures, in the sense that the restricted IORs form a consistent refinement structure linking apparently different domain-specific metrics into a single framework, or whether obstructions (e.g., prior dependence, non-monotonicity under environment-class inclusion) prevent such a unification.

Goal: produce theorems that either (a) establish concrete equivalences/refinements between the (restricted) IOR and existing intelligence/performance measures, or (b) demonstrate provable incompatibilities.
artifact.category_tag: Universal artificial intelligence / agent performance measures
artifact.status_search_result: The comparison between the Intelligence Order Relation (universal intelligence measure of Legg–Hutter) and conventional IQ tests or other domain-specific performance measures remains an active research direction; subsequent work (e.g., Hernández-Orallo and collaborators on anytime universal intelligence tests, and Hutter's later surveys) discusses partial connections but does not provide a definitive equivalence theorem. No publication appears to fully resolve the formal comparison or principled unification questions.

status_evidence.snippet: Lists comparison of IOR with IQ tests and restricted-class performance measures as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Measuring universal intelligence: Towards an anytime intelligence test
status_evidence.snippet: Hernández-Orallo and Dowe extend the Legg–Hutter measure but do not establish equivalence to IQ tests.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress only; full comparison remains unresolved.
